$comment: The second type-check project that is allowed to know a browser exists, and the first `apps/*` one. Root
tsconfig.json's own $comment (#259) says this is legal and names the three edits it obligates: a tsconfig
with `jsx`, one `tsc --noEmit -p` in the root `typecheck` script, and nothing else -- scripts/check-project.ts's
typecheck-coverage rule then holds the include lists in step, because it fails a source file claimed by no
project, one claimed by two projects, and a .tsx claimed only by projects that declare no `jsx`.
Why root `exclude` gained "apps/site" instead of this project claiming only the `.tsx` files: the root
program's globs are `apps/*/src/**/*.ts` and `apps/*/test/**/*.ts`, so a `.ts` here would sit in BOTH
programs -- two sets of `lib` answers for one file, which is exactly the failure that rule names. A
partition by extension would leave `site-config.ts` checked without `DOM`, and the one thing this app does
with the browser (read the config the deploy baked into the page) would be the thing that cannot compile.
What is overridden, and only this, mirroring packages/ui/tsconfig.json: `lib` gains DOM and DOM.Iterable,
`jsx` gains react-jsx, and `types` gains astro/client so `import.meta.env` is a type rather than a guess.
Every strictness flag -- `strict`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`,
`noUnusedLocals`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `erasableSyntaxOnly` -- comes from the root file through
`extends`, so this app is not held to a laxer standard than the server tree.
There is no workspace edge on `@platfolio/ui`, and that is a decision to flag rather than a default: the
island reaches the package through `astro.config.mjs`'s alias (and the `paths` entry below, which exists so
`tsc` answers the same question the bundler does). apps/control-plane declares four `workspace:*` edges, so
the edge is the convention here -- but a UI package that the shell may also reach by relative path does not
need a second mechanism, and an edge is a promise about who can import whom. The maintainer has not ruled on
whether the first-party shell is allowed to depend on `packages/ui` the way a service depends on a package;
this file takes the smaller commitment (alias only) and says so. If that ruling comes the other way, the
change is one line in package.json plus deleting the alias, and the gate in scripts/check-ui.ts that reads
the island's imports does not move.
`include` has no `.astro` entry: Astro compiles those itself and nothing here can type-check them. The build
is the gate for `.astro`, and `apps/site/test/build-output.test.ts` reads what the build emitted rather than
trusting this file.
